editorial.brief: Sara Bejlek appeared on Google Trends in India and the United States and in a Polymarket listing, the only name the feeds shared today. Elsewhere, Tom Skerritt led Wikipedia with 371,141 views, and a magnitude 7.0 quake near Nagqu, China topped 25 events of M2.5 or above.
editorial.cover_sub: Tom Skerritt led Wikipedia by a ratio of 1.1x over a singer named John Anderson, while two film titles and Elizabeth Holmes filled out the rest of the top five.
editorial.wiki_deck: Tom Skerritt drew 371,141 views, 34,562 more than John Anderson in second place. Nothing else in the snapshot says why.
editorial.letter_headline: A scattered day with one shared name
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is occupied with Docker and with machines checking software, Lemmy with a lost library and family, Bluesky with a Brazilian live stream and a Bauhaus weaving, Mastodon with bears, cats and disappointing hackers.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire ran on AI: a $100 million STEM pledge, a lawsuit over AI pricing, and graduate jobs in India. Britain searched for the weather, and Americans for Alabama and Auburn basketball.
editorial.markets_deck: Most of the board is politics and policy: a Fed hold at 94%, an Iran ceasefire at 98%, Flávio Bolsonaro at 77%, Netanyahu at 30%. Ethereum above $2,400 sits at 0%.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,219,364 players, ahead of Dota 2 at 973,555 and PUBG at 793,256. On Twitch, xQc held 20,454 viewers, with LacyOffline_ at 16,434.
editorial.yt_headline: The Rings of Power season three trailer
editorial.yt_note: Trailers and music videos hold the list: LISA at 1,966,537 views, a Mass Effect 5 trailer leak at 102,629, and a Minecraft Cold War simulation at 875,284.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow's edition, Sara Bejlek's double appearance will have thinned, the Iran ceasefire market dated October 22 will have expired, and the Ethereum market at 0% will be history. So will Skerritt's 371,141 views and the 7.0 near Nagqu as a headline number. The Docker post may linger.
wiki_paras: Tom Skerritt was the most-read article on Wikipedia in the snapshot, with 371,141 views. John Anderson, listed as a singer, followed with 336,579. The lead over second place is a ratio of 1.1x, which in a contest of this kind is a photo finish rather than a landslide.

Jailer 2 took third with 243,842 views, Elizabeth Holmes fourth with 182,703, and Clayface, marked as a film, fifth with 168,347. Jailer 2 has the look of a sequel, so a release calendar may be doing some of the work. The data does not say which release, or whether it touches Skerritt.

Neither Skerritt nor Anderson appears in any other feed. No Hacker News story, trending video or wire item points to a cause, so the reason stays with the readers who clicked. What the snapshot can report is that two names finished within 35,000 views of each other, which is as close as this list gets.
letter_paras: The snapshot found a scattered day. Only one topic appeared in more than one feed, and it was a name, Sara Bejlek, on Google Trends and in a prediction market.
